council_term: puḫru môʿidi / pḫr mʿd (“the assembled council”); bn ilm (“sons of El”)
presiding_figure: El, the aged father of the gods
members: The sons of El / the seventy sons of Athirat
function: El presides while the assembly debates and confers kingship (Baal, Yam, Mot contend)

council_term: ʿădat-ʾēl (“the divine council / assembly of El”)
members: The ʾĕlōhîm (“gods”), judged for unjust rule and sentenced to “die like men”
function: Judgment and demotion of the council gods

members: The host of heaven, standing on his right and left
function: Deliberation — a spirit volunteers as a “lying spirit” to entice Ahab

members: The sons of God, with ha-śāṭān (“the Accuser”) among them
function: The court presents itself; the wager over Job

council_term: bənê ʾĕlōhîm / bənê ʾēl (“sons of God,” LXX & 4QDeut)
members: The sons of God — one set over each nation; Yahweh's allotment is Israel
function: Division of the nations among the council members
Commissioning — “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” (the council plural)

council_term: puḫur ilāni (“the assembly of the gods”)
function: The assembly grants Marduk kingship and the Tablet of Destinies to fight Tiamat
The assembly decrees the flood under oath — a decision Enki argues against

council_term: The “Holy Ones” / the heavenly host before the throne
presiding_figure: The Great Glory / the Lord of Spirits
members: The Holy Ones; the Watchers (rebel members who descend)
function: The heavenly court; the archangels petition; judgment on the Watchers

council_term: The gods of heaven, in dynastic succession
presiding_figure: The reigning sky-king (Alalu → Anu → Kumarbi → Teshub)
function: The succession of divine kingship in heaven

source_text: Book of Moses / Book of Abraham
council_term: The “council in heaven”; the “noble and great ones”
members: The premortal spirits / the noble and great ones
function: The premortal council debates the plan and the choice of a Redeemer

members: Hera, Athena, Poseidon, Apollo, Themis, and the Olympian gods
function: The gods sit in assembly; Zeus raises whether to end or renew the war, Hera and Athena argue, and the destruction of Troy is resolved

source_text: The Contendings of Horus and Seth (Papyrus Chester Beatty I)
reference: Chester Beatty I (20th Dynasty, c. 1147 BCE)
members: Thoth, Isis, Geb, Neith, Atum, Shu
function: A divine tribunal adjudicates the eighty-year succession dispute over Osiris's throne between Horus and Seth

members: The assembled gods — the great gods and the commoner deities
function: Jupiter convenes the gods, denounces Lycaon and humankind, and the assembly assents to his resolve to destroy the human race by flood

council_term: rökstólar (‘seats of counsel’); the regin / ginnheilög goð
presiding_figure: The regin collectively; Odin in the Prose Edda
function: The gods take their seats of counsel — ordering time, resolving to fashion the dwarves, and deliberating the Æsir–Vanir war

council_term: ukkin (the assembly) — ‘the fifty great gods’ and ‘the seven who decree the fates’ (the Anunna)
presiding_figure: The assembly collectively (Enlil is the defendant, not the presider)
members: The fifty great gods; the seven Anunna who decree the fates
function: The divine assembly at Nippur seizes, judges, and banishes Enlil as ritually impure for defiling Ninlil

reference: Adi Parva, Sections XVII–XVIII (the churning of the ocean of milk)
council_term: devasabhā / sabhā (the conclave of the celestials)
members: The devas, assembled on Mount Meru
function: The celestials sit in conclave on Meru; Nārāyaṇa counsels Brahmā and they resolve to churn the ocean of milk for the amrita (the nectar of immortality)
